title: Register skills as Pydantic AI tools (Epic 4, issue #36)
prompt:
Register every skill as a Pydantic AI tool with Pydantic input models. Ensure validation rejects malformed payloads. Group debater vs controller skill sets.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: usage to be filled by main loop from harness report

note: Epic 4 final task (PRD §5.2/§5.3): wires the six existing skills (built in 4.1-4.4 as functions + Pydantic input models) onto the agents as REAL Pydantic AI tools, grouped into two disjoint sets. New module packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/agents/tools.py (141 code lines): two grouping factories debater_tools(settings=None, gatekeeper=None) -> list[Tool] and controller_tools() -> list[Tool]. Each skill is wrapped in a thin closure whose SINGLE argument is a Pydantic input model, then registered via pydantic_ai.Tool(fn, name=...) and passed to Agent(model, ..., tools=[...]) at construction — so pydantic-ai enforces validation at the tool boundary and a malformed payload raises ValidationError before the skill runs. Tool API used: pydantic-ai v1.104.0 Tool objects passed via Agent(tools=[...]); registered tools introspected through agent._function_toolset.tools (dict keyed by name) and each tool's input validator via tool.function_schema.validator.validate_python(payload). DEBATER set = [web_search, build_argument, analyze_opponent_argument] (DEBATER_SKILLS); CONTROLLER set = [assess_drift, nudge, render_verdict] (CONTROLLER_SKILLS) — tool names sourced from those skill-list constants + WEB_SEARCH_TOOL (no literal inlined), so names can never drift from what the system prompt advertises. web_search captures settings+gatekeeper in its closure and threads them through web_search(...), preserving the no-bypass property (every external call routes via the API gatekeeper, Epic 13). build_argument/analyze_opponent_argument already take Pydantic models so register directly; assess_drift/nudge/render_verdict take loose params so each gets a model-arg wrapper — added one new input model NudgeRequest(agent: DebateSide, reason: str) in skills/models.py (re-exported from skills + core), since nudge had no request model (DriftRequest/VerdictRequest/WebSearchInput already existed). Wired tools into create_debater (debater_tools, + optional gatekeeper kwarg threaded through create_pro_debater/create_con_debater) and create_controller (controller_tools); re-exported debater_tools/controller_tools from agent_debate.core.agents. TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_skill_tools.py (17 tests), watched it fail (ImportError: cannot import name 'controller_tools'), implemented to green. Tests assert: each agent has exactly its own three tools registered (set equality on introspected names); debater/controller sets are disjoint (no cross-wiring); tool names == DEBATER_SKILLS/CONTROLLER_SKILLS (match prompt); a malformed payload to every tool's input model raises ValidationError (incl. whitespace-only nudge reason hitting the strip validator). Existing agent tests stay green (tools attach with no network at construction; TestModel injection unchanged). Gates green locally: uv sync clean; ruff check . = All checks passed; ruff format --check . clean; mypy = no issues in 140 source files; pytest --cov = 539 passed, 100% on tools.py + models.py, 99.61% total (>=85 required); check_line_limit.py rc=0 (tools.py 141 code lines, under 150); secret_scan.py rc=0. NOT over-built: no full LLM tool-loop run (acceptance only needs tools REGISTERED + validation rejecting bad input), Gatekeeper left optional/None-defaulting per existing engine wiring.
